findings.failure_scenario: Sidecar workers run as a separate subprocess (SidecarSubProcess Popen's sidecar_worker.py, sidecar_subprocess.py:93-138), which instantiates SpotTerminationMonitorSidecar (sidecar_worker.py:59), and _monitor_loop runs in a multiprocessing Process forked from that worker. So getppid() inside _monitor_loop is the sidecar worker's pid. When the IMDS termination-time endpoint returns 200, the metadata is recorded but the SIGTERM kills only the sidecar worker; the user's task keeps running until AWS reclaims the instance (~2 min later), with no graceful shutdown or retry. Additionally, the worker's death breaks its stdin pipe, and SidecarSubProcess._send_internal (sidecar_subprocess.py:180-181) restarts the worker on the next message send, which re-runs _is_aws_spot_instance (still "spot") and re-records duplicate termination metadata until the instance dies.
findings.summary: os.kill(os.getppid(), SIGTERM) targets the sidecar worker subprocess, not the Metaflow task process, so the task is never notified of the imminent spot termination.

findings.failure_scenario: Line 193 seeds env = {"METAFLOW_FLOW_FILENAME": os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])}, but line 196 assigns env = env_deco[0].attributes["vars"] whenever the step has an @environment decorator (attributes["vars"] is {} even for a bare @environment). The pod then launches without METAFLOW_FLOW_FILENAME, so in the sidecar flow_filename is None and it runs `python /metaflow/None spot-metadata record ...`, which fails with 'can't open file'; the termination metadata is never registered for any flow using @environment(vars=...), a very common kubernetes configuration, and the failure is only a print to the sidecar's stderr.
findings.summary: The env dict is replaced wholesale by the @environment decorator's vars, silently dropping the newly added METAFLOW_FLOW_FILENAME for any step with @environment.

findings.failure_scenario: MetaflowEnvironment.get_package_commands (metaflow_environment.py:162-175) runs `mkdir metaflow; cd metaflow; ... tar xf job.tar`, so the flow file lands at $WORKDIR/metaflow/<filename>, where $WORKDIR is the image's default working directory (neither kubernetes.py/kubernetes_job.py nor argo_workflows.py sets working_dir in the pod spec). The hardcoded /metaflow/<filename> is correct only when the image workdir is /. With any custom image that sets WORKDIR (e.g., WORKDIR /root, common with @kubernetes(image=...)/@argo), the record subprocess fails with [Errno 2] No such file or directory, and the spot-termination metadata is silently never recorded.
findings.summary: The sidecar hardcodes the absolute path /metaflow/{flow_filename}, but the runtime bootstrap extracts the code package to a metaflow/ directory relative to the container's working directory, which no pod spec in this repo sets.

findings.failure_scenario: _monitor_loop calls _emit_termination_metadata, which runs `python <flow> spot-metadata record ...` with subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True) and no timeout. If the metadata CLI blocks (e.g., a slow or unreachable metadata service whose client retries for a long time, or local-metadata lock contention), the run never returns, os.kill(os.getppid(), SIGTERM) at line 74 never executes, and the task keeps running unaware of the termination notice until AWS forcibly reclaims the instance; even on the correct target process, the entire graceful-shutdown mechanism hinges on an unbounded external call.
findings.summary: subprocess.run has no timeout and the SIGTERM to the parent is sequenced after it, so a hang in the spot-metadata CLI permanently blocks the termination signal.

findings.failure_scenario: The --tag option is declared required=False with default=None, so running `python flow.py spot-metadata record --run-id 1 --step-name start --task-id 2 --termination-notice-time 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z` without --tag passes tags=None into validate_tags, whose first statement is frozenset(tags) (tagging_util.py:42), raising an unhandled TypeError. The defensive `tag_list = list(tags) if tags else []` on the next line is never reached; the CLI advertises tags as optional but crashes when they are omitted.
findings.summary: validate_tags(tags) is called before the None-guard, so invoking record without --tag crashes with TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable.

findings.failure_scenario: _get_imds_token swallows RequestException and returns None, so _make_ec2_request sends the GET without the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header. On a spot instance in a cluster with IMDSv2 enforced (HttpTokens=required, a recommended AWS hardening), or on a transient 1s-timeout of the token PUT during the sidecar's first second of life, the instance-life-cycle request returns 401, _is_aws_spot_instance returns False, the monitor process is never started, and there is no retry: the task runs with the spot-termination feature silently absent and gets force-terminated by AWS.
findings.summary: A single-shot IMDS token failure at startup silently disables the monitor on clusters that enforce IMDSv2, because the headerless fallback GET returns 401 and _is_aws_spot_instance gives up.

findings.failure_scenario: current._update_env (metaflow_current.py:65-67) only sets a property on the current class object; a repo-wide grep shows no reader of spot_termination_notice anywhere, and SpotTerminationMonitorSidecar hardcodes "/tmp/spot_termination_notice" when opening the file (which itself is written but never consumed). The env-var/file indirection misleads future maintainers into thinking the notice path is configurable or observed, and the write of the file plus the per-task _update_env call are wasted work on every Kubernetes task.
findings.summary: current._update_env({"spot_termination_notice": "/tmp/spot_termination_notice"}) is dead code: nothing ever reads current.spot_termination_notice, and the notice file the sidecar writes is never read either.
